H1.d: a primitive word; father, in a literal and immediate, or figurative and remote application; chief, (fore-) father(-less), [idiom] patrimony, principal. Compare names in 'Abi-'.

H3.d: from the same as אָבִיב; a green plant; greenness, fruit.

H4.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אֵב; {a green plant}; fruit.

H5.d: of foreign origin; Abagtha, a eunuch of Xerxes; Abagtha.

H6.d: a primitive root; properly, to wander away, i.e. lose oneself; by implication to perish (causative, destroy); break, destroy(-uction), [phrase] not escape, fail, lose, (cause to, make) perish, spend, [idiom] and surely, take, be undone, [idiom] utterly, be void of, have no way to flee.

H7.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אָבַד; {properly, to wander away, i.e. lose oneself; by implication to perish (causative, destroy)}; destroy, perish.

H8.d: active of participle of אָבַד; (concrete) wretched or (abstract) destruction; perish.

H9.d: from אָבַד; Compare אֲבַדֹּה.; concrete, something lost; abstract, destruction, i.e. Hades; lost.

H10.d: the same as אֲבֵדָה, miswritten for אֲבַדּוֹן; a perishing; destruction.

H11.d: intensive from אָבַד; abstract, a perishing; concrete, Hades; destruction.

H14.d: a primitive root; to breathe after, i.e. (figuratively) to be acquiescent; consent, rest content will, be willing.

H16.d: from אָבָה (in the sense of bending toward); the papyrus; swift.

H17.d: from אָבָה (in the sense of desiring); want; sorrow.

H18.d: from אָבַס; a manger or stall; crib.

H19.d: from an unused root (apparently meaning to turn); brandishing of a sword; point.

H20.d: of uncertain derivation; a melon (only plural); melon.

H21.d: from אָב; fatherly; Abi, Hezekiah's mother; Abi.

H22.d: from אָב and אֵל; father (i.e. possessor) of God; Abiel, the name of two Israelites; Abiel.

H23.d: from אָב and אָסַף; father of gathering (i.e. gatherer); Abiasaph, an Israelite; Abiasaph.

H24.d: from an unused root (meaning to be tender); green, i.e. a young ear of grain; hence, the name of the month Abib or Nisan; Abib, ear, green ears of corn (not maize).

H25.d: from אָב and גִּבְעוֹן; father (i.e. founder) of Gibon; Abi-Gibon, perhaps an Israelite; father of Gibeon.

H26.d: or shorter אֲבִיגַל; from אָב and גִּיל; father (i.e. source) of joy; Abigail or Abigal, the name of two Israelitesses; Abigal.

H27.d: from אָב and דִּין; father of judgment (i.e. judge); Abidan, an Israelite; Abidan.

H28.d: from אָב and יָדַע; father of knowledge (i.e. knowing); Abida, a son of Abraham by Keturah; Abida, Abidah.

H29.d: or prolonged אֲבִיָּהוּ ; from אָב and יָהּ; father (i.e. worshipper) of Jah; Abijah, the name of several Israelite men and two Israelitesses; Abiah, Abijah.

H30.d: from אָב and הוּא; father (i.e. worshipper) of Him (i.e. God); Abihu, a son of Aaron; Abihu.

H31.d: from אָב and הוֹד; father (i.e. possessor) of renown; Abihud, the name of two Israelites; Abihud.

H32.d: or (more correctly) אֲבִיחַיִל ; from אָב and חַיִל; father (i.e. possessor) of might; Abihail or Abichail, the name of three Israelites and two Israelitesses; Abihail.

H33.d: from אֲבִיעֶזֶר with the article inserted; father of the Ezrite; an Abiezrite or descendant of Abiezer; Abiezrite.

H34.d: from אָבָה, in the sense of want (especially in feeling); destitute; beggar, needy, poor (man).

H35.d: from אָבָה; provocative of desire; the caper berry (from its stimulative taste); desire.

H36.d: from אָב and טוּב; father of goodness (i.e. good); Abitub, an Israelite; Abitub.

H37.d: from אָב and טַל; father of dew (i.e. fresh); Abital, a wife of King David; Abital.

H38.d: from אָב and יָם; father of (the) sea (i.e. seaman); Abijam (or Abijah), a king of Judah; Abijam.

H39.d: from אָב and an elsewhere unused (probably foreign) word; father of Mael (apparently some Arab tribe); Abimael, a son of Joktan; Abimael.

H40.d: from אָב and מֶלֶךְ; father of (the) king; Abimelek, the name of two Philistine kings and of two Israelites; Abimelech.

H41.d: from אָב and נָדַב; father of generosity (i.e. liberal); Abinadab, the name of four Israelites; Abinadab.

H42.d: from אָב and נֹעַם; father of pleasantness (i.e. gracious); Abinoam, an Israelite; Abinoam.

H43.d: contracted from אֲבִיאָסָף; Ebjasaph, an Israelite; Ebiasaph.

H44.d: from אָב and עֵזֶר; father of help (i.e. helpful); Abiezer, the name of two Israelites; Abiezer.

H45.d: from אָב and an unused root of uncertain derivation; probably, father of strength (i.e. valiant); Abialbon, an Israelite; Abialbon.

H46.d: from אָבַר; mighty (spoken of God); mighty (one).

H47.d: for אָבִיר; {mighty (spoken of God)}; angel, bull, chiefest, mighty (one), stout(-hearted), strong (one), valiant.

H48.d: from אָב and רוּם; father of height (i.e. lofty); Abiram, the name of two Israelites; Abiram.

H49.d: from אָב and שָׁגָה; father of error (i.e. blundering); Abishag, a concubine of David; Abishag.

H50.d: xlit ʼĂbîyshûwac corrected to ʼĂbîyshûwaʻ; from אָב and שׁוֹעַ; father of plenty (i.e. prosperous); Abishua, the name of two Israelites; Abishua.

H51.d: from אָב and שׁוּר; father of (the) wall (i.e. perhaps mason); Abishur, an Israelite; Abishur.

H52.d: or (shorter) אַבְשַׁי ; from אָב and שַׁי; father of a gift (i.e. probably generous); Abishai, an Israelite; Abishai.

H53.d: or (shortened) אַבְשָׁלוֹם ; from אָב and שָׁלוֹם; father of peace (i.e. friendly); Abshalom, a son of David; also (the fuller form) a later Israelite; Abishalom, Absalom.

H54.d: contracted from אָב and יָתַר; father of abundance (i.e. liberal); Ebjathar, an Israelite; Abiathar.

H55.d: a primitive root; probably to coil upward; mount up.

H56.d: a primitive root; to bewail; lament, mourn.

H58.d: from an unused root (meaning to be grassy); a meadow; plain. Compare also the proper names beginning with Abel-.

H59.d: from אָבֵל; a meadow; Abel, the name of two places in Palestine.; Abel.

H61.d: apparently from אָבַל through the idea of negation; nay, i.e. truly or yet; but, indeed, nevertheless, verily.

H62.d: from אָבֵל and בַּיִת and מַעֲכָה; meadow of Beth-Maakah; Abel of Beth-maakah, a place in Palestine; Abel-beth-maachah, Abel of Beth-maachah,

H63.d: from אָבֵל and the plural of שִׁטָּה, with the article inserted; meadow of the acacias; Abel hash-Shittim, a place in Palestine; Abelshittim.

H64.d: from אָבֵל and the plural of כֶּרֶם; meadow of vineyards; Abel-Keramim, a place in Palestine; plain of the vineyards.

H65.d: from אָבֵל and מְחֹלָהxlit mᵉchôwlâh corrected to mᵉchôlâh; meadow of dancing; Abel-Mecholah, a place in Palestine; Abel-meholah.

H66.d: from אָבֵל and מַיִם; meadow of water; Abel-Majim, a place in Palestine; Abel-maim.

H67.d: from אָבֵל and מִצְרַיִם; meadow of Egypt; Abel-Mitsrajim, a place in Palestine; Abel-mizraim.

H68.d: from the root of בָּנָה through the meaning to build; a stone; [phrase] carbuncle, [phrase] mason, [phrase] plummet, (chalk-, hail-, head-, sling-) stone(-ny), (divers) weight(-s).

H70.d: from the same as אֶבֶן; a pair of stones (only dual); a potter's wheel or a midwife's stool (consisting alike of two horizontal disks with a support between); wheel, stool.

H71.d: perhaps feminine of אֶבֶן; stony;  Compare אֲמָנָה.; Abanah, a river near Damascus; Abana.

H72.d: from אֶבֶן and עֵזֶר with the article inserted; stone of the help; Eben-ha-Ezer, a place in Palestine; Ebenezer.

H73.d: of uncertain derivation; a belt; girdle.

H74.d: or (fully) אֲבִינֵר ; from אָב and נִיר; father of light (i.e. enlightening); Abner, an Israelite; Abner.

H75.d: a primitive root; to fodder; fatted, stalled.

H76.d: (by reduplication) from an unused root (meaning to belch forth); an inflammatory pustule (as eruption); blains.

H77.d: from an unused root probably meaning to gleam; conspicuous; Ebets, a place in Palestine; Abez.

H78.d: from the same as אֲבַעְבֻּעָה; splendid; Ibtsan, an Israelite; Ibzan.

H79.d: a primitive root, probably to float away (as vapor), but used only as denominative from אָבָק; to bedust, i.e. grapple; wrestle.

H80.d: from root of אָבַק; light particles (as volatile); (small) dust, powder.

H81.d: feminine of אָבָק; {light particles (as volatile)}; powder.

H82.d: a primitive root; to soar; fly.

H84.d: feminine of אֵבֶר; {a pinion}; feather, wing.

H85.d: contracted from אָב and an unused root (probably meaning to be populous); father of a multitude; Abraham, the later name of Abram; Abraham.

H86.d: probably an Egyptian word meaning; kneel; bow the knee.

H87.d: contracted from אֲבִירָם; high father; Abram, the original name of Abraham; Abram.

H88.d: plural of אוֹב; water-skins; Oboth, a place in the Desert; Oboth.

H89.d: of uncertain derivation (compare אֲגַג); Age, an Israelite; Agee.

H90.d: or אֲגָג; of uncertain derivation (compare אָגֵא); flame; Agag, a title of Amalekitish kings; Agag.

H91.d: patrial or patronymic from אֲגַג; an Agagite or descendent (subject) of Agag; Agagite.

H92.d: feminine passive participle of an unused root (meaning to bind); a band, bundle, knot, or arch; bunch, burden, troop.

H93.d: prob of Persian origin; a nut; nut.

H94.d: passive participle of אָגַר; gathered (i.e. received among the sages); Agur, a fanciful name for Solomon; Agur.

H95.d: from the same as אָגוּר; properly, something gathered, i.e. perhaps a grain or berry; used only of a small (silver) coin; piece (of) silver.

H96.d: from an unused root (meaning to flow down or together as drops); a reservoir; drop.

H97.d: dual of אֶגֶל.; a double pond; Eglajim, a place in Moab; Eglaim.

H98.d: from an unused root (meaning to collect as water); a marsh; hence a rush (as growing in swamps); hence a stockade of reeds; pond, pool, standing (water).

H99.d: probably from the same as אֲגַם (in the sense of stagnant water); figuratively, sad; pond.

H100.d: from the same as אֲגַם; a marshy pool (others from a different root, a kettle); by implication; a bulrush (as growing there); collectively a rope of bulrushes; bulrush, caldron, hook, rush.

H101.d: probably from נָגַן; a bowl (as pounded out hollow); basin, cup, goblet.

H102.d: probably from נָגַף (through the idea of impending); a cover or heap; i.e.; (only plural) wings of an army, or crowds of troops; bands.

H103.d: a primitive root; to harvest; gather.

H104.d: (Aramaic) of Persian origin; an epistle (as carried by a state courier or postman); letter.

H105.d: of uncertain derivation; a basin; charger.

H106.d: from גָּרַף (in the sense of grasping); the clenched hand; fist.

H107.d: feminine of אִגְּרָא; an epistle; letter.

H108.d: from the same as אוּד (in the sense of enveloping); a fog; mist, vapor.

H109.d: a primitive root; to languish; grieve.

H110.d: probably from אָדַב (in the sense of chastisement) and אֵל; disciplined of God; Adbeel, a son of Ishmael; Adbeel.

H111.d: probably an orthographical variation for חֲדַד; Adad (or Hadad), an Edomite; Hadad.

H112.d: of uncertain derivation; Iddo, an Israelite; Iddo.

H113.d: or (shortened) אָדֹן; from an unused root (meaning to rule); sovereign, i.e. controller (human or divine); lord, master, owner. Compare also names beginning with 'Adoni-'.

H114.d: probably intensive for אָדוֹן; powerful; Addon, apparently an Israelite; Addon.

H115.d: dual from אָדַר (in the sense of eminence); double mound; Adorajim, a place in Palestine; Adoraim.

H116.d: (Aramaic) of uncertain derivation; then (of time); now, that time, then.

H117.d: from אָדַר; wide or (generally) large; figuratively, powerful; excellent, famous, gallant, glorious, goodly, lordly, mighty(-ier one), noble, principal, worthy.

H118.d: of Persian derivation; Adalja, a son of Haman; Adalia.

H119.d: to show blood (in the face), i.e.; flush or turn rosy; be (dyed, made) red (ruddy).

H120.d: from אָדַם; ruddy i.e. a human being (an individual or the species, mankind, etc.); [idiom] another, [phrase] hypocrite, [phrase] common sort, [idiom] low, man (mean, of low degree), person.

H121.d: the same as אָדָם; Adam the name of the first man, also of a place in Palestine; Adam.

H123.d: or (fully) אֱדוֹם ; from אָדֹם; red (see Genesis 25:25); Edom, the elder twin-brother of Jacob; hence the region (Idumaea) occupied by him; Edom, Edomites, Idumea.

H124.d: from אָדַם; redness, i.e. the ruby, garnet, or some other red gem; sardius.

H126.d: contracted for אֲדָמָה; earthy; Admah, a place near the Dead Sea; Admah.

H127.d: from אָדַם; soil (from its general redness); country, earth, ground, husband(-man) (-ry), land.

H128.d: the same as אֲדָמָה; Adamah, a place in Palestine; Adamah.

H129.d: from אֲדָמָה; earthy; Adami, a place in Palestine; Adami.

H130.d: or (fully) אֱדוֹמִי ; patronymic from אֱדֹם; See אֲרוֹמִי.; an Edomite, or descendants from (or inhabitants of) Edom; Edomite.

H131.d: plural of אָדָם; red spots; Adummim, a pass in Palestine; Adummim.

H132.d: or (fully) אַדְמוֹנִי ; from אָדַם; reddish (of the hair or the complexion); red, ruddy.

H133.d: probably of Persian derivation; Admatha, a Persian nobleman; Admatha.

H134.d: from the same as אָדוֹן (in the sense of strength); a basis (of a building, a column, etc.); foundation, socket.

H135.d: intensive from the same as אֶדֶן; firm; Addan, an Israelite; Addan.

H136.d: an emphatic form of אָדוֹן; the Lord (used as a proper name of God only); (my) Lord.

H137.d: from אָדוֹן and בֶּזֶק; lord of Bezek; Adoni-Bezek; a Canaanitish king; Adonibezek.

H138.d: original (prolonged) אֲדֹנִיָּהוּ ; from אָדוֹן and יָהּ; lord (i.e. worshipper) of Jah; Adonijah, the name of three Israelites; Adonijah.

H139.d: from אָדוֹן and צֶדֶק; lord of justice; Adoni-Tsedek, a Canaanitish king; Adonizedec.

H140.d: from אָדוֹן and קוּם; lord of rising (i.e. high); Adonikam, the name of one or two Israelites; Adonikam.

H141.d: from אָדוֹן and רוּם; lord of height; Adoniram, an Israelite; Adoniram.

H142.d: a primitive root; to expand, i.e. be great or (figuratively) magnificent; (become) glorious, honourable.

H143.d: probably of foreign derivation; perhaps meaning fire; Adar, the 12th Hebrew month; Adar.

H144.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אֲדָר; {Adar, the 12th Hebrew month}; Adar.

H145.d: from אָדַר; amplitude, i.e. (concrete) a mantle; also (figuratively) splendor; goodly, robe.

H146.d: intensive from אָדַר; ample; Addar, a place in Palestine; also an Israelite; Addar.

H147.d: (Aramaic) intensive, from a root corresponding to אָדַר; ample, i.e. a threshing-floor; threshingfloor.

H148.d: (Aramaic) from the same as אִדַּר, and גְּזַר; a chief diviner, or astrologer; judge.

H149.d: (Aramaic) probably of Persian origin; quickly or carefully; diligently.

H150.d: of Persian origin; a daric or Persian coin; dram.

H151.d: contracted for אֲדֹנִירָם; Adoram (or Adoniram), an Israelite; Adoram.

H152.d: from אָדַר and מֶלֶךְ; splendor of (the) king; Adrammelek, the name of an Assyrian idol, also of a son of Sennacherib; Adrammelech.

H153.d: (Aramaic) an orthographical variation for דְּרַע; an arm, i.e. (figuratively) power; force.

H154.d: from the equivalent of אֶדְרָע; mighty; Edrei, the name of two places in Palestine; Edrei.

H155.d: feminine of אַדִּיר; ; also the same as אֶדֶר; something ample (as a large vine, a wide dress); garment, glory, goodly, mantle, robe.

H156.d: a primitive root; to tread out (grain); thresh.

H157.d: or אָהֵב ; a primitive root; to have affection for (sexually or otherwise); (be-) love(-d, -ly, -r), like, friend.

H158.d: from אָהַב; affection (in a good or a bad sense); love(-r).

H159.d: from אָדַשׁ; meaning the same as אַהַב; {affection (in a good or a bad sense)}; love.

H160.d: feminine of אַהַב and meaning the same; {affection (in a good or a bad sense)}; love.

H161.d: from an unused root meaning to be united; unity; Ohad, an Israelite; Ohad.

H162.d: apparently a primitive word expressing pain exclamatorily; Oh!; ah, alas.

H163.d: probably of foreign origin; Ahava, a river of Babylonia; Ahava.

H164.d: from the same as אֹהַד; united; Ehud, the name of two or three Israelites; Ehud.

H165.d: apparently an orthographical variation for אַיֵּה; where; I will be (Hosea 13:10,14) (which is often the rendering of the same Hebrew form from הָיָה).

H166.d: a primitive root; to be clear; shine.

H167.d: a denominative from אֹהֶל; to tent; pitch (remove) a tent.

H168.d: from אָהַל; a tent (as clearly conspicuous from a distance); covering, (dwelling) (place), home, tabernacle, tent.

H169.d: the same as אֹהֶל; Ohel, an Israelite; Ohel.

H170.d: in form a feminine of אֹהֶל, but in fact for אׇהֳלָהּ; from אֹהֶל; her tent (i.e. idolatrous sanctuary); Oholah, a symbolic name for Samaria; Aholah.

H171.d: from אֹהֶל and אָב; tent of (his) father; Oholiab, an Israelite; Aholiab.

H172.d: (similarly with אׇהֳלָה) for אׇהֳלִיבָהּ ; from אֹהֶל; my tent (is) in her; Oholibah, a symbolic name for Judah; Aholibah.

H173.d: from אֹהֶל and בָּמָה; tent of (the) height; Oholibamah, a wife of Esau; Aholibamah.

H174.d: or (feminine) אֲהָלוֹת (only used thus in the plural); of foreign origin; aloe wood (i.e. sticks); (tree of lign-) aloes.

H175.d: of uncertain derivation; Aharon, the brother of Moses; Aaron.

H176.d: presumed to be the 'constructive' or genitival form of אַו ; short for אַוָּה; desire (and so probably in Proverbs 31:4); hence (by way of alternative) or, also if; also, and, either, if, at the least, [idiom] nor, or, otherwise, then, whether.

H177.d: from אוֹ and אֵל; wish of God; Uel, and Israelite; Uel.

H178.d: from the same as אָב (apparently through the idea of prattling a father's name); properly, a mumble, i.e. a water skin (from its hollow sound); hence a necromancer (ventriloquist, as from a jar); bottle, familiar spirit.

H179.d: probably from אָבַל; mournful; Obil, an Ishmaelite; Obil.

H180.d: or (shortened) אֻבָל ; from יָבַל (in the sense of יָבָל); a stream; river.

H181.d: from an unused root meaning to rake together; a poker (for turning or gathering embers); (fire-) brand.

H182.d: or (shortened) אֹדוֹת (only thus in the plural); from the same as אוּד; turnings (i.e. occasions); (adverb) on account of; (be-) cause, concerning, sake.

H183.d: a primitive root; to wish for; covet, (greatly) desire, be desirous, long, lust (after).

H184.d: a primitive root; to extend or mark out; point out.

H185.d: from אָוָה; longing; desire, lust after, pleasure.

H186.d: perhaps by permutation for עֻזִּי, strong; Uzai, an Israelite; Uzai.

H187.d: of uncertain derivation; Uzal, a son of Joktan; Uzal.

H188.d: probably from אָוָה (in the sense of crying out after); lamentation; also interjectionally Oh!; alas, woe.

H189.d: probably from אָוָה; desirous; Evi, a Midianitish chief; Evi.

H190.d: feminine of אוֹי; {lamentation; also interjectionally Oh!}; woe.

H191.d: from an unused root (meaning to be perverse); (figuratively) silly; fool(-ish) (man).

H192.d: of Aramaic derivation and probably meaning soldier of Merodak; Evil-Merodak, a Babylonian king; Evil-merodach.

H193.d: from an unused root meaning to twist, i.e. (by implication) be strong; the body (as being rolled together); also powerful; mighty, strength.

H194.d: or (shortened) אֻלַי; from אוֹ; if not; hence perhaps; if so be, may be, peradventure, unless.

H195.d: of Persian derivation; the Ulai (or Eulaeus), a river of Persia; Ulai.

H196.d: from אֱוִיל; silly, foolish; hence (morally) impious; foolish.

H197.d: or (shortened), אֻלָם ; from אָלַם (in the sense of tying); a vestibule (as bound to the building); porch.

H198.d: appar, from אָלַם (in the sense of dumbness); solitary; Ulam, the name of two Israelites; Ulam.

H199.d: apparently a variation of אוּלַי; however or on the contrary; as for, but, howbeit, in very deed, surely, truly, wherefore.

H200.d: from the same as אֱוִיל; silliness; folly, foolishly(-ness).

H201.d: from אָמַר; talkative; Omar, a grandson of Esau; Omar.

H202.d: probably from the same as אָוֶן (in the sense of effort, but successful); ability, power, (figuratively) wealth; force, goods, might, strength, substance.

H203.d: the same as אוֹן; On, an Israelite; On.

H204.d: or (shortened); אֹן; of Egyptian derivation; On, a city of Egypt; On.

H205.d: from an unused root perhaps meaning properly, to pant (hence, to exert oneself, usually in vain; to come to naught); strictly nothingness; also trouble. vanity, wickedness; specifically an idol; affliction, evil, false, idol, iniquity, mischief, mourners(-ing), naught, sorrow, unjust, unrighteous, vain, vanity, wicked(-ness). Compare אַיִן.

H206.d: the same as אָוֶן; idolatry; Aven, the contemptuous synonym of three places, one in Coele-Syria, one in Egypt (On), and one in Palestine (Bethel); Aven. See also אוֹן, בֵּית אָוֶן.

H207.d: or (shortened) אֹנוֹ; prolonged from אוֹן; strong; Ono, a place in Palestine; Ono.

H208.d: a variation of אוֹנָן; strong; Onam, the name of an Edomite and of an Israelite; Onam.

H209.d: a variation of אוֹנוֹ; strong; Onan, a son of Judah; Onan.

H210.d: perhaps a corruption of אוֹפִיר; Uphaz, a famous gold region; Uphaz.

H211.d: or (shortened) אֹפִיר; and אוֹפִר; of uncertain derivation; Ophir, the name of a son of Joktan, and of a gold region in the East; Ophir.

H212.d: or (shortened) אֹפָן; from an unused root meaning to revolve; a wheel; wheel.

H213.d: a primitive root; to press; (by implication) to be close, hurry, withdraw; (make) haste(-n, -y), labor, be narrow.

H214.d: from אָצַר; a depository; armory, cellar, garner, store(-house), treasure(-house) (-y).

H215.d: a primitive root; to be (causative, make) luminous (literally and metaphorically); [idiom] break of day, glorious, kindle, (be, en-, give, show) light (-en, -ened), set on fire, shine.

H216.d: from אוֹר; illumination or (concrete) luminary (in every sense, including lightning, happiness, etc.); bright, clear, [phrase] day, light (-ning), morning, sun.

H217.d: from אוֹר; flame; hence (in the plural) the East (as being the region of light); fire, light. See also אוּרִים.

H218.d: the same as אוּר; Ur, a place in Chaldaea; also an Israelite; Ur.

H219.d: feminine of אוֹר; luminousness, i.e. (figuratively) prosperity; also a plant (as being bright); herb, light.

H220.d: by transposition for אֻרְוָה; a stall; cote.

H221.d: from אוּר; fiery; Uri, the name of three Israelites; Uri.

H222.d: from אוּר and אֵל; flame of God; Uriel, the name of two Israelites; Uriel.

H223.d: or (prolonged) אוּרִיָּהוּ ; from אוּר and יָהּ; flame of Jah; Urijah, the name of one Hittite and five Israelites; Uriah, Urijah.

H224.d: plural of אוּר; lights; Urim, the oracular brilliancy of the figures in the high-priest's breastplate; Urim.

H225.d: a primitive root; properly, to come, i.e. (implied) to assent; consent.

H226.d: probably from אוּת (in the sense of appearing); a signal (literally or figuratively), as aflag, beacon, monument, omen, prodigy, evidence, etc.; mark, miracle, (en-) sign, token.

H227.d: a demonstrative adverb; at that time or place; also as a conjunction, therefore; beginning, for, from, hitherto, now, of old, once, since, then, at which time, yet.

H228.d: (Aramaic) or אֲזָה (Aramaic); to kindle; (by implication) to heat; heat, hot.

H229.d: probably from אֵזוֹב; hyssop-like; Ezbai, an Israelite; Ezbai.

H230.d: (Aramaic) of uncertain derivation; firm; be gone.

H231.d: probably of foreign derivation; hyssop; hyssop.

H232.d: from אֲזִקִּים; something girt; a belt, also a band; girdle.

H233.d: probably from אָז; at that time; then.

H234.d: from זָכַר; a reminder; specifically remembrance-offering; memorial.

H235.d: a primitive root; to go away, hence, to disappear; fail, gad about, go to and fro (but in Ezekiel 27:19 the word is rendered by many 'from Uzal,' by others 'yarn'), be gone (spent).

H236.d: (Aramaic) the same as אָזַל; to depart; go (up).

H237.d: from אָזַל; departure; Ezel, a memorial stone in Palestine; Ezel.

H238.d: a primitive root; probably to expand; but used only as a denominative from אֹזֶן; to broaden out the ear (with the hand), i.e. (by implication) to listen; give (perceive by the) ear, hear(-ken). See אָזַן.

H239.d: a primitive root (rather identical with אָזַן through the idea of scales as if two ears); to weigh, i.e. (figuratively) ponder; give good heed.

H240.d: from אָזַן; a spade or paddle (as having a broad end); weapon.

H241.d: from אָזַן; broadness. i.e. (concrete) the ear (from its form in man); [phrase] advertise, audience, [phrase] displease, ear, hearing, [phrase] show.

H242.d: from אָזַן and שֶׁאֱרָה; plot of Sheerah (i.e. settled by him); Uzzen-Sheerah, a place in Palestine; Uzzen-sherah.

H243.d: from אָזַן and תָּבוֹר; flats (i.e. tops) of Tabor (i.e. situated on it); Aznoth-Tabor, a place in Palestine; Aznoth-tabor.

H244.d: from אֹזֶן; having (quick) ears; Ozni, an Israelite; also an Oznite (collectively), his descendant; Ozni, Oznites.

H245.d: from אָזַן and יָהּ; heard by Jah; Azanjah, an Israelite; Azaniah.

H246.d: a variation for זִיקָה; manacles; chains.

H247.d: a primitive root; to belt; bind (compass) about, gird (up, with).

H248.d: a variation for זְרוֹעַ; the arm; arm.

H249.d: from זָרַח (in the sense of springing up); a spontaneous growth, i.e. native (tree or persons); bay tree, (home-) born (in the land), of the (one's own) country (nation).

H250.d: patronymic from חֹבָב; an Ezrachite or descendant of Zerach; Ezrahite.

H251.d: a primitive word; a brother (used in the widest sense of literal relationship and metaphorical affinity or resemblance (like father)); another, brother(-ly); kindred, like, other. Compare also the proper names beginning with 'Ah-' or 'Ahi-'.

H252.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אָח; {a brother (used in the widest sense of literal relationship and metaphorical affinity or resemblance)}; brother.

H253.d: a variation for אֲהָהּ; Oh! (expressive of grief or surprise); ah, alas.

H254.d: of uncertain derivation; a fire-pot or chafing dish; hearth.

H255.d: probably from אָח; a howler or lonesome wild animal; doleful creature.

H256.d: once (by contraction) אֶחָב (Jeremiah 29:22); from אָח and אָב; brother (i.e. friend) of (his) father; Achab, the name of a king of Israel and of a prophet at Babylon; Ahab.

H257.d: from אָח and בִּין; brother (i.e. possessor) of understanding; Achban, an Israelite; Ahban.

H258.d: perhaps a primitive root; to unify, i.e. (figuratively) collect (one's thoughts); go one way or other.

H259.d: a numeral from אָחַד; properly, united, i.e. one; or (as an ordinal) first; a, alike, alone, altogether, and, any(-thing), apiece, a certain, (dai-) ly, each (one), [phrase] eleven, every, few, first, [phrase] highway, a man, once, one, only, other, some, together,

H260.d: of uncertain (perhaps Egyptian) derivation; a bulrush or any marshy grass (particularly that along the Nile); flag, meadow.

H261.d: from אָחַד; united; Echud, the name of three Israelites; Ehud.

H262.d: from חָוָה (in the sense of חֲוָא); an utterance; declaration.

H263.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אַחְוָה; solution (of riddles); showing.

H265.d: by reduplication from אָח; brotherly; Achoach, an Israelite; Ahoah.

H266.d: patronymic from אַחֲוָה; an Achochite or descendant of Achoach; Ahohite.

H267.d: perhaps from אָח and מַיִם; brother (i.e. neighbour) of water; Achumai, an Israelite; Ahumai.

H268.d: or (shortened) אָחֹר ; from אֲחִירַע; the hinder part; hence (adverb) behind, backward; also (as facing north) the West; after(-ward), back (part, -side, -ward), hereafter, (be-) hind(-er part), time to come, without.

H269.d: irregular feminine of אָח; a sister (used very widely (like brother), literally and figuratively); (an-) other, sister, together.

H270.d: a primitive root; to seize (often with the accessory idea of holding in possession); [phrase] be affrighted, bar, (catch, lay, take) hold (back), come upon, fasten, handle, portion, (get, have or take) possess(-ion).

H271.d: from אָחַז; possessor; Achaz, the name of a Jewish king and of an Israelite; Ahaz.

H272.d: feminine passive participle from אָחַז; something seized, i.e. a possession (especially of land); possession.

H273.d: from אָחַז; seizer; Achzai, an Israelite; Ahasai.

H274.d: or (prolonged) אֲחַזְיָהוּ ; from אָחַז and יָהּ; Jah has seized; Achazjah, the name of a Jewish and an Israelite king; Ahaziah.

H275.d: from אָחַז; seizure; Achuzzam, an Israelite; Ahuzam.

H276.d: a variation of אֲחֻזָּה; possession; Achuzzath, a Philistine; Ahuzzath.

H277.d: from אָח; brotherly; Achi, the name of two Israelites; Ahi.

H278.d: probably the same as אֲחִי; Echi, an Israelite; Ehi.

H279.d: from אָח and אֵם; brother of the mother (i.e. uncle); Achiam, an Israelite; Ahiam.

H280.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to חִידָה,; an enigma; hard sentence.

H281.d: or (prolonged) אֲחִיָּהוּ ; from אָח and יָהּ; brother (i.e. worshipper) of Jah; Achijah, the name of nine Israelites; Ahiah, Ahijah.

H282.d: from אָח and הוֹד; brother (i.e. possessor) of renown; Achihud, an Israelite; Ahihud.

H283.d: prolonged from אָח; brotherly; Achio, the name of three Israelites; Ahio.

H284.d: from אָח and חוּד; brother of a riddle (i.e. mysterious); Achichud, an Israelite; Ahihud.

H285.d: from אָח and טוּב; brother of goodness; Achitub, the name of several priests; Ahitub.

H286.d: from אָח and יָלַד; brother of one born; Achilud, an Israelite; Ahilud.

H287.d: from אָח and מוּת; brother of death; Achimoth, an Israelite; Ahimoth.

H288.d: from אָח and מֶלֶךְ; brother of (the) king; Achimelek, the name of an Israelite and of a Hittite; Ahimelech.

H289.d: or אֲחִימָן ; from אָח and מִן; brother of a portion (i.e. gift); Achiman, the name of an Anakite and of an Israelite; Ahiman.

H290.d: from אָח and the equivalent of מַעַץ; brother of anger; Achimaats, the name of three Israelites; Ahimaaz.

H291.d: from אָח; brotherly; Achjan, an Israelite; Ahian.

H292.d: from אָח and נָדַב; brother of liberality; Achinadab, an Israelite; Ahinadab.

H293.d: from אָח and נֹעַם; brother of pleasantness; Achinoam, the name of two Israelitesses; Ahinoam.

H294.d: from אָח and סָמַךְ; brother of support; Achisamak, an Israelite; Ahisamach.

H295.d: from אָח and עֵזֶר; brother of help; Achiezer, the name of two Israelites; Ahiezer.

H296.d: from אָח and קוּם; brother of rising (i.e. high); Achikam, an Israelite; Ahikam.

H297.d: from אָח and רוּם; brother of height (i.e. high); Achiram, an Israelite; Ahiram.

H298.d: patronymic from אֲחִירָם; an Achiramite or descendant (collectively) of Achiram; Ahiramites.

H299.d: from אָח and רַע; brother of wrong; Achira, an Israelite; Ahira.

H300.d: from אָח and שַׁחַר; brother of (the) dawn; Achishachar, an Israelite; Ahishar.

H301.d: from אָח and שִׁיר; brother of (the) singer; Achishar, an Israelite; Ahishar.

H302.d: from אָח and תָּפֵל; brother of folly; Achithophel, an Israelite; Ahithophel.

H303.d: from the same root as חֶלֶב; fatness (i.e. fertile); Achlab, a place in Palestine; Ahlab.

H304.d: the same as אַחֲלַי; wishful; Achlai, the name of an Israelitess and of an Israelite; Ahlai.

H305.d: or אַחֲלֵי; prob from אָח and a variation of לוּא; would that!; O that, would God.

H306.d: perhaps from חָלַם (and thus dream-stone); a gem, probably the amethyst; amethyst.

H307.d: of Persian derivation; Achmetha (i.e. Ecbatana), the summer capital of Persia; Achmetha.

H308.d: of uncertain derivation; Achasbai, an Israelite; Ahasbai.

H309.d: a primitive root; to loiter (i.e. be behind); by implication to procrastinate; continue, defer, delay, hinder, be late (slack), stay (there), tarry (longer).

H310.d: from אָחַר; properly, the hind part; generally used as an adverb or conjunction, after (in various senses); after (that, -ward), again, at, away from, back (from, -side), behind, beside, by, follow (after, -ing), forasmuch, from, hereafter, hinder end, [phrase] out (over) live, [phrase] persecute, posterity, pursuing, remnant, seeing, since, thence(-forth), when, with.

H312.d: from אָחַר; properly, hinder; generally, next, other, etc.; (an-) other man, following, next, strange.

H313.d: the same as אַחֵר; Acher, an Israelite; Aher.

H314.d: or (shortened) אַחֲרֹן; from אָחַר; hinder; generally, late or last; specifically (as facing the east) western; after (-ward), to come, following, hind(-er, -ermost, -most), last, latter, rereward, ut(ter) most.

H315.d: from אַחַר and אָח; after (his) brother; Achrach, an Israelite; Aharah.

H316.d: from אַחַר and חֵיל; behind (the) intrenchment (i.e. safe); Acharchel, an Israelite; Aharhel,

H318.d: (Aramaic) or (shortened) אׇחֳרֵן; (Aramaic) from אׇחֳרִי; last; at last.

H319.d: from אַחַר; the last or end, hence, the future; also posterity; (last, latter) end (time), hinder (utter) -most, length, posterity, remnant, residue, reward.

H320.d: (Aramaic) from אַחַר; the same as אַחֲרִית; later; latter.

H321.d: (Aramaic) from אַחַר; the same as אׇחֳרִי; other; (an-) other.

H322.d: prolonged from אָחוֹר; backwards; back (-ward, again).

H323.d: of Persian derivation; a satrap or governorof amain province (of Persia); lieutenant.

H324.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אֲחַשְׁדַּרְפַּן; {a satrap or governorof amain province (of Persia)}; prince.

H325.d: or (shortened) אַחַשְׁרֹשׁ (Esther 10:1); of Persian origin; Achashverosh (i.e. Ahasuerus or Artaxerxes, but in this case Xerxes), the title (rather than name) of a Persian king; Ahasuerus.

H326.d: probably of Persian derivation; an achastarite (i.e. courier); the designation (rather than name) of an Israelite; Haakashtari (includ. the article).

H327.d: of Persian origin; a mule; camel.

H328.d: from an unused root perhaps meaning to move softly; (as a noun) a necromancer (from their soft incantations), (as an adverb) gently; charmer, gently, secret, softly.

H329.d: from an unused root probably meaning to pierce or make fast; a thorn-tree (especially the buckthorn); Atad, bramble, thorn.

H330.d: from an unused root (probably meaning to bind); properly, twisted (yarn), i.e. tapestry; fine linen.

H331.d: a primitive root; to close (the lips or ears); by analology to contract (a window by bevelled jambs); narrow, shut, stop.

H332.d: a primitive root; to close up; shut.

H333.d: from אָטַר; maimed; Ater, the name of three Israelites; Ater.

H334.d: from אָטַר; shut up, i.e. impeded (as to the use of the right hand); [phrase] left-handed.

H335.d: perhaps from אַיִן; where? hence how?; how, what, whence, where, whether, which (way).

H336.d: lemma אי missing vowel, corrected to אִי; probably identical with אַי (through the idea of a query); not; island (Job 22:30).

H338.d: probably identical with אִי (through the idea of a doleful sound); a howler (used only in the plural), i.e. any solitary wild creature; wild beast of the islands.

H339.d: from אָוָה; properly, a habitable spot (as desirable); dry land, a coast, an island; country, isle, island.

H340.d: a primitive root; to hate (as one of an opposite tribe or party); hence to be hostile; be an enemy.

H341.d: or (fully) אוֹיֵב; active participle of אָיַב; hating; an adversary; enemy, foe.

H343.d: from the same as אוּד (in the sense of bending down); oppression; by implication misfortune, ruin; calamity, destruction.

H344.d: perhaps from אִי; the screamer, i.e. a hawk; kite, vulture.

H345.d: the same as אַיָּה; Ajah, the name of two Israelites; Aiah, Ajah.

H347.d: from אָיַב; hated (i.e. persecuted); Ijob, the patriarch famous for his patience; Job.

H348.d: from אִיlemma אי missing vowel, corrected to אִי and זְבֻל; Izebel, the wife of king Ahab; Jezebel.

H349.d: also אֵיכָה ; and אֵיכָכָה ; prolonged from אַי; how? or how!; also where; how, what.

H350.d: from אִיlemma אי missing vowel, corrected to אִי and כָּבוֹד; (there is) no glory, i.e. inglorious; Ikabod, a son of Phineas; I-chabod.

H351.d: probably a variation for אֵיךְ, but not as an interogative; where; where.

H352.d: from the same as אוּל; properly, strength; hence, anything strong; specifically a chief (politically); also a ram (from his strength); a pilaster (as a strong support); an oak or other strong tree; mighty (man), lintel, oak, post, ram, tree.

H353.d: a variation of אַיִל; strength; strength.

H354.d: an intensive form of אַיִל (in the sense of ram); a stag or male deer; hart.

H355.d: feminine of אַיָּל; a doe or female deer; hind.

H356.d: or (shortened) אֵלוֹן ; or אֵילֹן ; from אַיִל; oak-grove; Elon, the name of a place in Palestine, and also of one Hittite, two Israelites; Elon.

H357.d: from אַיָּל; deer-field; Ajalon, the name of five places in Palestine; Aijalon, Ajalon.

H358.d: from אֵילוֹן, בַּיִת, and חָנַן; oak-grove of (the) house of favor; Elon of Beth-chanan, a place in Palestine; Elon-bethhanan.

H359.d: or אֵילַת ; from אַיִל; trees or a grove (i.e. palms); Eloth or Elath, a place on the Red Sea; Elath, Eloth.

H360.d: feminine of אֱיָל; power; by implication, protection; strength.

H361.d: or (shortened) אֵלָם ; or (feminine) אֵלַמָּה ; probably from אַיִל; a pillar-space (or colonnade), i.e. a pale (or portico); arch.

H362.d: plural of אַיִל; palm-trees; Elim, a place in the Desert; Elim.

H363.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אֵילוֹן; a tree; tree.

H364.d: from אַיִל and פָּארָן; oak of Paran; El-Paran, a portion of the district of Paran; El-paran.

H365.d: the same as אַיָּלָה; a doe; hind, Aijeleth.

H366.d: from an unused root (meaning to frighten); frightful; terrible.

H367.d: or (shortened) אֵמָה; from the same as אָיֹם; fright; concrete, an idol (as a bugbear); dread, fear, horror, idol, terrible, terror.

H368.d: plural of אֵימָה; terrors; Emim, an early Canaanitish (or Maobitish) tribe; Emims.

H369.d: as if from a primitive root meaning to be nothing or not exist; a non-entity; generally used as a negative particle; else, except, fail, (father-) less, be gone, in(-curable), neither, never, no (where), none, nor, (any, thing), not, nothing, to nought, past, un(-searchable), well-nigh, without. Compare אַיִן.

H370.d: probably identical with אַיִן in the sense of query (compare אִיlemma אי missing vowel, corrected to אִי); where? (only in connection with prepositional prefix, whence); whence, where.

H371.d: apparently a shortened form of אַיִן; but (like אַיִן) an interrogative; is it not?; not.

H372.d: from אִיlemma אי missing vowel, corrected to אִי and עֵזֶר; helpless; Iezer, an Israelite; Jeezer.

H373.d: patronymic from אִיעֶזֵר; an Iezrite or descendant of Iezer; Jezerite.

H374.d: or (shortened) אֵפָה ; of Egyptian derivation; an ephah or measure for grain; hence, a measure in general; ephah, (divers) measure(-s).

H375.d: from אַי and פֹּה; what place?; also (of time) when?; or (of means) how?; what manner, where.

H376.d: contracted for אֱנוֹשׁ (or perhaps rather from an unused root meaning to be extant); a man as an individual or a male person; often used as an adjunct to a more definite term (and in such cases frequently not expressed in translation); also, another, any (man), a certain, [phrase] champion, consent, each, every (one), fellow, (foot-, husband-) man, (good-, great, mighty) man, he, high (degree), him (that is), husband, man(-kind), [phrase] none, one, people, person, [phrase] steward, what (man) soever, whoso(-ever), worthy. Compare אִשָּׁה.

H377.d: denominative from אִישׁ; to be a man, i.e. act in amanly way; show (one) self a man.

H378.d: from אִישׁ and בֹּשֶׁת; man of shame; Ish-Bosheth, a son of King Saul; Ish-bosheth.

H379.d: from אִישׁ and הוֹד; man of renown; Ishod, an Israelite; Ishod.

H380.d: diminutive from אִישׁ; the little man of the eye; the pupil or ball; hence, the middle (of night); apple (of the eye), black, obscure.

H381.d: from אִישׁ and חַיִל; man of might; by defective transcription (2 Samuel 23:20) אִישׁ־חַיxlit ʼÎsh-Chay corrected to ʼÎysh-Chay; as if from אִישׁ and חַי; living man; Ishchail (or Ish-chai), an Israelite; a valiant man.

H382.d: from אִישׁ and טוֹב; man of Tob; Ish-Tob, a place in Palestine; Ish-tob.

H383.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to יֵשׁ; properly, entity; used only as aparticle of affirmation, there is; art thou, can, do ye, have, it be, there is (are), [idiom] we will not.

H384.d: perhaps from אֹשֶׁר and אֵל; God has arrived; Ithiel, the name of an Israelite, also of a symbolical person; Ithiel.

H385.d: from אִי and תָּמָר; coast of the palm-tree; Ithamar, a son of Aaron; Ithamar.

H386.d: or (shortened) אֵתָן ; from an unused root (meaning to continue); permanence; hence (concrete) permanent; specifically a chieftain; hard, mighty, rough, strength, strong.

H387.d: the same as אֵיתָן; permanent; Ethan, the name of four Israelites; Ethan.

H388.d: plural of אֵיתָן; always with the article; the permanent brooks; Ethanim, the name of a month; Ethanim.

H389.d: akin to אָכֵן; a particle of affirmation, surely; hence (by limitation) only; also, in any wise, at least, but, certainly, even, howbeit, nevertheless, notwithstanding, only, save, surely, of a surety, truly, verily, [phrase] wherefore, yet (but).

H390.d: from an unused root probably meaning to strengthen; a fortress; Accad, a place in Babylon; Accad.

H391.d: from כָּזַב; falsehood; by implication treachery; liar, lie.

H392.d: from אַכְזָב; deceitful (in the sense of a winter-torrent which fails in summer); Akzib, the name of two places in Palestine; Achzib.

H393.d: from an unused root (apparently meaning to act harshly); violent; by implication deadly; also (in a good sense) brave; cruel, fierce.

H396.d: feminine from אָכַל; something eatable, i.e. food; meat.

H397.d: of uncertain derivation; Akish, a Philistine king; Achish.

H398.d: a primitive root; to eat (literally or figuratively); [idiom] at all, burn up, consume, devour(-er, up), dine, eat(-er, up), feed (with), food, [idiom] freely, [idiom] in...wise(-deed, plenty), (lay) meat, [idiom] quite.

H399.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אָכַל; {to eat (literally or figuratively)}; [phrase] accuse, devour, eat.

H400.d: from אָכַל; food; eating, food, meal(-time), meat, prey, victuals.

H401.d: or אֻכָּל; apparently from אָכַל; devoured; Ucal, a fancy name; Ucal.

H402.d: feminine of אֻכָל; food; consume, devour, eat, food, meat.

H403.d: from כּוּן (compare כֵּן); firmly; figuratively, surely; also (advers.) but; but, certainly, nevertheless, surely, truly, verily.

H404.d: a primitive root; apparently meaning to curve (as with a burden); to urge; crave.

H405.d: from אָכַף; a load; by implication, a stroke (others dignity); hand.

H406.d: from an unused root meaning to dig; a farmer; husbandman, ploughman.

H407.d: from כָּשַׁף; fascination; Acshaph, a place in Palestine; Achshaph.

H408.d: a negative particle (akin to לֹא); not (the qualified negation, used as a deprecative); once (Job 24:25) as a noun, nothing; nay, neither, [phrase] never, no, nor, not, nothing (worth), rather than.

H409.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אַל; {not (the qualified negation, used as a deprecative); once (Job 24:25) as a noun, nothing}; not.

H410.d: shortened from אַיִל; strength; as adjective, mighty; especially the Almighty (but used also of any deity); God (god), [idiom] goodly, [idiom] great, idol, might(-y one), power, strong. Compare names in '-el.'

H411.d: a demonstrative particle (but only in a plural sense); these or those; these, those. Compare אֵלֶּה.

H412.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אֵל; {these or those}; these.

H413.d: (but only used in the shortened constructive form אֶל ); a primitive particle; properly, denoting motion towards, but occasionally used of a quiescent position, i.e.; near, with or among; often in general, to; about, according to, after, against, among, as for, at, because(-fore, -side), both...and, by, concerning, for, from, [idiom] hath, in(-to), near, (out) of, over, through, to(-ward), under, unto, upon, whether, with(-in).

H414.d: a variation of אֵלָהlemma אִלָה first vowel, corrected to אֵלָה; oak; Ela, an Israelite; Elah.

H415.d: from אֵל and אֱלֹהִים and יִשְׂרָאֵל; the mighty god if Jisrael; El-Elohi-Jisrael, the title given to a consecrated spot by Jacob; Elelohe-israel.

H416.d: from אֵל and בֵּית־אֵל; the God of Bethel; El-Bethel, the title given to a consecrated spot by Jacob; El-beth-el.

H417.d: from אֵל and גָּבִישׁ; hail (as if a great pearl); great hail(-stones).

H418.d: by transposition for אַלְמֻגִּים; sticks of algum wood; algum (trees).

H419.d: from אֵל and דּוֹד; God has loved; Eldad, an Israelite; Eldad.

H420.d: from אֵל and יָדַע; God of knowledge; Eldaah, a son of Midian; Eldaah.

H421.d: a primitive root (rather identical with אָלָה through the idea of invocation); to bewail; lament.

H422.d: a primitive root; properly, to adjure, i.e. (usually in a bad sense) imprecate; adjure, curse, swear.

H423.d: from אָלָה; an imprecation; curse, cursing, execration, oath, swearing.

H424.d: lemma אִלָה first vowel, corrected to אֵלָה; feminine of אַיִל; an oak or other strong tree; elm, oak, teil-tree.

H425.d: the same as אֵלָהlemma אִלָה first vowel, corrected to אֵלָה; Elah, the name of an Edomite, of four Israelites, and also of a place in Palestine; Elah.

H426.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אֱלוֹהַּ; God; God, god.

H427.d: A variation of אֵלָהlemma אִלָה first vowel, corrected to אֵלָה; {an oak or other strong tree}; oak.

H428.d: prolonged from אֵל; these or those; an-(the) other; one sort, so, some, such, them, these (same), they, this, those, thus, which, who(-m).

H429.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אֵלֶּה; {these or those}; these.

H430.d: plural of אֱלוֹהַּ; gods in the ordinary sense; but specifically used (in the plural thus, especially with the article) of the supreme God; occasionally applied by way of deference to magistrates; and sometimes as a superlative; angels, [idiom] exceeding, God (gods) (-dess, -ly), [idiom] (very) great, judges, [idiom] mighty.

H431.d: (Aramaic) probably prolonged from אֵל; lo!; behold.

H432.d: probably from אַל; nay, i.e. (softened) if; but if, yea though.

H433.d: rarely (shortened) אֱלֹהַּ; probably prolonged (emphatic) from אֵל; a deity or the Deity; God, god. See אֱלֹהִים.

H434.d: for אֱלִיל; good for nothing; thing of nought.

H435.d: probably of foreign derivation; Elul, the sixth Jewish month; Elul.

H436.d: prolonged from אַיִל; an oak or other strong tree; plain. See also אֵילוֹן.

H437.d: a variation of אֵלוֹן; {an oak or other strong tree}; oak.

H438.d: the same as אַלּוֹן; Allon, an Israelite, also a place in Palestine; Allon.

H439.d: from אַלּוֹן and a variation of בְּכִית; oak of weeping; Allon-Bakuth, a monumental tree; Allon-bachuth.

H440.d: or rather (shortened) אֵלֹנִי; patron from אַלּוֹן; an Elonite or descendant (collectively) of Elon; Elonites.

H441.d: or (shortened) אַלֻּף; from אָלַף; familiar; a friend, also gentle; hence, a bullock (as being tame; applied, although masculine, to a cow); and so, a chieftain (as notable, like neat cattle); captain, duke, (chief) friend, governor, guide, ox.

H442.d: of uncertain derivation; Alush, a place in the Desert; Alush.

H443.d: from אֵל and זָבַד; God has bestowed; Elzabad, the name of two Israelites; Elzabad.

H444.d: a primitive root; to muddle, i.e. (figuratively and intransitive) to turn (morally) corrupt; become filthy.

H445.d: from אֵל and חָנַן; God (is) gracious; Elchanan, an Israelite; Elkanan.

H446.d: from אֵל and אָב; God of (his) father; Eliab, the name of six Israelites; Eliab.

H447.d: from אֵל repeated; God of (his) God; Eliel, the name of nine Israelites; Eliel.

H448.d: or (contraction) אֱלִיָּתָה; from אֵל and אוּת; God of (his) consent; Eliathah, an Israelite; Eliathah.

H449.d: from the same as אֶלְדָּד; God of (his) love; Elidad, an Israelite; Elidad.

H450.d: from אֵל and יָדַע; God (is) knowing; Eljada, the name of two Israelites and of an Aramaean leader; Eliada.

H451.d: from אָלָה (in the original sense of strength); the stout part, i.e. the fat tail of the Oriental sheep; rump.

H452.d: or prolonged אֵלִיָּהוּ; from אֵל and יָהּ; God of Jehovah; Elijah, the name of the famous prophet and of two other Israelites; Elijah, Eliah.

H453.d: or (fully) אֱלִיהוּא; from אֵל and הוּא; God of him; Elihu, the name of one of Job's friends, and of three Israelites; Elihu.

H454.d: or (shortened) אֶלְיוֹעֵינַי; from אֵל and יְהֹוָה and עַיִן; towards Jehovah (are) my eyes; Eljehoenai or Eljoenai, the name of seven Israelites; Elihoenai, Elionai.

H455.d: from אֵל and חָבָא; God will hide; Eljachba, an Israelite; Eliahbah.

H456.d: from אֵל and חֹרֶף; God of autumn; Elichoreph, an Israelite; Elihoreph.

H457.d: apparently from אַל; good for nothing, by anal. vain or vanity; specifically an idol; idol, no value, thing of nought.

H458.d: from אֵל and מֶלֶךְ; God of (the) king; Elimelek, an Israelite; Elimelech.

H459.d: (Aramaic) or shorter אִלֵּן; prolonged from אֵל; these; the, these.

H460.d: from אֵל and יָסַף; God (is) gatherer; Eljasaph, the name of two Israelites; Eliasaph.

H461.d: from אֵל and עֵזֶר; God of help; Eliezer, the name of a Damascene and of ten Israelites; Eliezer.

H462.d: probably contracted for אֶלְיְהוֹעֵינַי; Elienai, an Israelite; Elienai.

H463.d: from אֵל and עַם; God of (the) people; Eliam, an Israelite; Eliam.

H464.d: from אֵל and פָּז; God of gold; Eliphaz, the name of one of Job's friends, and of a son of Esau; Eliphaz.

H465.d: from אֵל and פָּלַל; God of judgment; Eliphal, an Israelite; Eliphal.

H466.d: from אֵל and פָּלָה; God of his distinction; Eliphelehu, an Israelite; Elipheleh.

H467.d: or (shortened) אֱלְפֶּלֶט; from אֵל and פַּלֵּט; God of deliverance; Eliphelet or Elpelet, the name of six Israelites; Eliphalet, Eliphelet, Elpalet.

H468.d: xlit ʼĔlêytsûwr corrected to ʼĔlîytsûwr; from אֵל and צוּר; God of (the) rock; Elitsur, an Israelite; Elizur.

H469.d: or (shortened) אֶלְצָפָן; from אֵל and צָפַן; God of treasure; Elitsaphan or Eltsaphan, an Israelite; Elizaphan, Elzaphan.

H470.d: from אֵל and קוֹא; God of rejection; Elika, an Israelite; Elika.

H471.d: from אֵל and קוּם; God of raising; Eljakim, the name of four Israelites; Eliakim.

H472.d: from אֵל and שֶׁבַע (in the sense of שָׁבַע); God of (the) oath; Elisheba, the wife of Aaron; Elisheba.

H473.d: probably of foreign derivation; Elishah, a son of Javan; Elishah.

H474.d: from אֵל and שׁוּעַ; God of supplication (or of riches); Elishua, the son of King David; Elishua.

H475.d: from אֵל and שׁוּב; God will restore; Eljashib, the name of six Israelites; Eliashib.

H476.d: from אֵל and שָׁמַע; God of hearing; Elishama, the name of seven Israelites; Elishama.

H477.d: contracted for אֱלִישׁוּעַ.; Elisha, the famous prophet; Elisha.

H478.d: from אֵל and שָׁפַט; God of judgment; Elishaphat, an Israelite; Elishaphat.

H479.d: (Aramaic) prolonged from אֵל; these; these, those.

H480.d: by reduplication from אָלָה; alas!; woe.

H481.d: a primitive root; to tie fast; hence (of the mouth) to be tongue-tied; bind, be dumb, put to silence.

H482.d: from אָלַם; silence (i.e. mute justice); congregation. Compare יוֹנַת אֵלֶם רְחֹקִים.

H484.d: probably of foreign derivation (used thus only in the plural); almug (i.e. probably sandle-wood) sticks; almug trees. Compare אַלְגּוּמִּים.

H485.d: or (masculine) אָלֻם; passive participle of אָלַם; something bound; a sheaf; sheaf.

H486.d: probably of foreign derivation; Almodad, a son of Joktan; Almodad.

H487.d: from אַלָּה and מֶלֶךְ; oak of (the) king; Allammelek, a place in Palestine; Alammelech.

H488.d: prolonged from אָלַם in the sense of bereavement; discarded (as a divorced person); forsaken.

H489.d: from אָלַם as in אַלְמָן; bereavement; widowhood.

H490.d: feminine of אַלְמָן; a widow; also a desolate place; desolate house (palace), widow.

H491.d: feminine of אַלְמָן; concrete, a widow; abstract, widowhood; widow, widowhood.

H492.d: from אַלְמֹן in the sense of concealment; some one (i.e. so and so, without giving the name of the person or place); one, and such.

H493.d: from אֵל and נָעֵם; God (is his) delight; Elnaam, an Israelite; Elnaam.

H494.d: from אֵל and נָתַן; God (is the) giver; Elnathan, the name of four Israelites; Elnathan.

H495.d: probably of foreign derivation; Ellasar, an early country of Asia; Ellasar.

H496.d: from אֵל and עוּד; God has testified; Elad, an Israelite; Elead.

H497.d: from אֵל and עָדָה; God has decked; Eladah, an Israelite; Eladah.

H498.d: from אֵל and עוּז (in the sense of עֹז); God (is) defensive; Eluzai, an Israelite; Eluzai.

H499.d: from אֵל and עָזַר; God (is) helper; Elazar, the name of seven Israelites; Eleazar.

H500.d: or (more properly) אֶלְעָלֵה; from אֵל and עָלָה; God (is) going up; Elale or Elaleh, a place east of the Jordan; Elealeh.

H501.d: from אֵל and עָשָׂה; God has made; Elasah, the name of four Israelites; Elasah, Eleasah.

H502.d: a primitive root, to associate with; hence, to learn (and causatively to teach); learn, teach, utter.

H503.d: denominative from אֶלֶף; causative, to make athousandfold; bring forth thousands.

H504.d: from אָלַף; a family; also (from the sense of yoking or taming) an ox or cow; family, kine, oxen.

H505.d: prop, the same as אֶלֶף; hence (the ox's head being the first letter of the alphabet, and this eventually used as a numeral) a thousand; thousand.

H506.d: (Aramaic) or אֶלֶף; (Aramaic), corresponding to אֶלֶף; {hence (the ox's head being the first letter of the alphabet, and this eventually used as a numeral) a thousand}; thousand.

H507.d: the same as אֶלֶף; Eleph, a place in Palestine; Eleph.

H508.d: from אֵל and פָּעַל; God (is) act; Elpaal, an Israelite; Elpaal.

H509.d: a primitive root; to press; urge.

H510.d: probably from אַל and קוּם; a non-rising (i.e. resistlessness); no rising up.

H511.d: from אֵל and קָנָה; God has obtained; Elkanah, the name of several Israelites; Elkanah.

H512.d: patrial from a name of uncertain derivation; an Elkoshite or native of Elkosh; Elkoshite.

H513.d: probably from אֵל and a masculine form of תּוֹלְדָה (compare תּוֹלָד); God (is) generator; Eltolad, a place in Palestine; Eltolad.

H514.d: xlit ʼEltᵉqê corrected to ʼEltᵉqêʼ; or (more properly) אֶלְתְּקֵה; of uncertain derivation; Eltekeh or Elteke, a place in Palestine; Eltekeh.

H515.d: from אֵל and תָּקַן; God (is) straight; Eltekon, a place in Palestine; Eltekon.

H516.d: from אַל and שָׁחַת; 'Thou must not destroy'; probably the opening words to a popular song; Al-taschith.

H517.d: a primitive word; a mother (as the bond of the family); in a wide sense (both literally and figuratively (like father)); dam, mother, [idiom] parting.

H518.d: a primitive particle; used very widely as demonstrative, lo!; interrogative, whether?; or conditional, if, although; also Oh that!, when; hence, as a negative, not; (and, can-, doubtless, if, that) (not), [phrase] but, either, [phrase] except, [phrase] more(-over if, than), neither, nevertheless, nor, oh that, or, [phrase] save (only, -ing), seeing, since, sith, [phrase] surely (no more, none, not), though, [phrase] of a truth, [phrase] unless, [phrase] verily, when, whereas, whether, while, [phrase] yet.

H519.d: apparently a primitive word; a maidservant or female slave; (hand-) bondmaid(-woman), maid(-servant).

H520.d: prolonged from אֵם; properly, a mother (i.e. unit of measure, or the fore-arm (below the elbow), i.e. a cubit; also a door-base (as a bond of the entrance); cubit, [phrase] hundred (by exchange for מֵאָה), measure, post.

H521.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אַמָּה; {properly, a mother (i.e. unit of measure, or the fore-arm (below the elbow), i.e. a cubit; also a door-base (as a bond of the entrance)}; cubit.

H522.d: the same as אַמָּה; Ammah, a hill in Palestine; Ammah.

H523.d: from the same as אֵם; a collection, i.e. community of persons; nation, people.

H524.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אֻמַּה; {a collection, i.e. community of persons}; nation.

H525.d: from אָמַן, probably in the sense of training; like אָמָן; skilled, i.e. an architect; one brought up.

H526.d: the same as אָמוֹן; Amon, the name of three Israelites; Amon.

H527.d: a variation for הָמוֹן; a throng of people; multitude.

H528.d: of Egyptian derivation; used only as an adjunct of נֹא; Amon (i.e. Ammon or Amn), a deity of Egypt; multitude, populous.

H529.d: from אָמַן; established, i.e. (figuratively) trusty; also (abstractly) trustworthiness; faith(-ful), truth.

H530.d: or (shortened) אֱמֻנָה; feminine of אֵמוּן; literally firmness; figuratively security; morally fidelity; faith(-ful, -ly, -ness, (man)), set office, stability, steady, truly, truth, verily.

H531.d: from אָמַץ; strong; Amots, an Israelite; Amoz.

H532.d: an abbreviated form for אָמוֹן; Ami, an Israelite; Ami.

H533.d: or (shortened) אַמִּץ; from אָמַץ; strong or (abstractly) strength; courageous, mighty, strong (one).

H534.d: apparently from אָמַר (in the sense of self-exaltation); a summit (of a tree or mountain); bough, branch.

H535.d: a primitive root; to droop; by implication to be sick, to mourn; languish, be weak, wax feeble.

H538.d: from אֵם; gathering-spot; Amam, a place in Palestine; Amam.

H539.d: a primitive root; (Isaiah 30:21; interchangeable with אָמַן, to go to the right hand); properly, to build up or support; to foster as a parent or nurse; figuratively to render (or be) firm or faithful, to trust or believe, to be permanent or quiet; morally to be true or certain; hence, assurance, believe, bring up, establish, [phrase] fail, be faithful (of long continuance, stedfast, sure, surely, trusty, verified), nurse, (-ing father), (put), trust, turn to the right.

H540.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אָמַן; {properly, to build up or support; to foster as a parent or nurse; figuratively to render (or be) firm or faithful, to trust or believe, to be permanent or quiet; morally to be true or certain}; believe, faithful, sure.

H541.d: denominative from יָמִין; to take the right hand road; turn to the right. See אָמַן.

H542.d: from אָמַן (in the sense of training); an expert; cunning workman.

H543.d: from אָמַן; sure; abstract, faithfulness; adverb, truly; Amen, so be it, truth.

H545.d: feminine of אֹמֶן (in the specific sense of training); tutelage; brought up.

H546.d: feminine form of אֹמֶן (in its usual sense); adverb, surely; indeed.

H547.d: feminine active participle of אֹמֶן (in the original sense of supporting); a column; pillar.

H548.d: feminine of אָמֵן; something fixed, i.e. a covenant. an allowance; certain portion, sure.

H549.d: the same as אֲמָנָה; Amanah, a mountain near Damascus; Amana.

H550.d: or אֲמִינוֹן; from אָמַן; faithful; Amnon (or Aminon), a son of David; Amnon.

H551.d: adverb from אֹמֶן; verily; indeed, no doubt, surely, (it is, of a) true(-ly, -th).

H552.d: an orthographical variation of אׇמְנָם; {verily}; in (very) deed; of a surety.

H553.d: a primitive root; to be alert, physically (on foot) or mentally (in courage); confirm, be courageous (of good courage, stedfastly minded, strong, stronger), establish, fortify, harden, increase, prevail, strengthen (self), make strong (obstinate, speed).

H554.d: probably from אָמַץ; of a strong color, i.e. red (others fleet); bay.

H557.d: from אָמַץ; strong; Amtsi, an Israelite; Amzi.

H558.d: or אֲמַצְיָהוּ; from אָמַץ and יָהּ; strength of Jah; Amatsjah, the name of four Israelites; Amaziah.

H559.d: a primitive root; to say (used with great latitude); answer, appoint, avouch, bid, boast self, call, certify, challenge, charge, [phrase] (at the, give) command(-ment), commune, consider, declare, demand, [idiom] desire, determine, [idiom] expressly, [idiom] indeed, [idiom] intend, name, [idiom] plainly, promise, publish, report, require, say, speak (against, of), [idiom] still, [idiom] suppose, talk, tell, term, [idiom] that is, [idiom] think, use (speech), utter, [idiom] verily, [idiom] yet.

H560.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אָמַר; {to say (used with great latitude)}; command, declare, say, speak, tell.

H561.d: from אָמַר; something said; answer, [idiom] appointed unto him, saying, speech, word.

H562.d: the same as אֵמֶר; {something said}; promise, speech, thing, word.

H563.d: (Aramaic) perhaps from אֲמַר (in the sense of bringing forth); a lamb; lamb.

H564.d: from אָמַר; talkative; Immer, the name of five Israelites; Immer.

H565.d: or אֶמְרָה; feminine of אֵמֶר, and meaning the same; {something said}; commandment, speech, word.

H566.d: from אִמֵּר; Imri, the name of two Israelites; Imri.

H567.d: probably a patronymic from an unused name derived from אָמַר in the sense of publicity, i.e. prominence; thus, a mountaineer; an Emorite, one of the Canaanitish tribes; Amorite.

H568.d: or prolonged אֲמַרְיָהוּ; from אָמַר and יָהּ; Jah has said (i.e. promised); Amarjah, the name of nine Israelites; Amariah.

H569.d: of uncertain (perhaps foreign) derivation; Amraphel, a king of Shinar; Amraphel.

H570.d: time past, i.e.; yesterday or last night; former time, yesterday(-night)

H571.d: contracted from אָמַן; stability; (figuratively) certainty, truth, trustworthiness; assured(-ly), establishment, faithful, right, sure, true (-ly, -th), verity.

H572.d: from מָתַח; properly, something expansive, i.e. a bag; sack.

H573.d: from אֶמֶת; veracious; Amittai, an Israelite; Amittai.

H574.d: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to that of מֹתֶן; well-loined (i.e. burly) or mighty; terrible.

H575.d: or אָנָה; contracted from אַיִן; where?; hence, whither?, when?; also hither and thither; [phrase] any (no) whither, now, where, whither(-soever).

H576.d: (Aramaic) or אֲנָה; (Aramaic), corresponding to אֲנִיlemma אֲנַי second vowel, corrected to אֲנִי; I; I, as for me.

H577.d: lemma אָנּאָ second vowel, corrected to אָנָּא; or אָנָּה; apparent contracted from אַהֲבָה and נָא; oh now!; I (me) beseech (pray) thee, O.

H578.d: a primitive root; to groan; lament, mourn.

H579.d: a primitive root (perhaps rather identical with אָנָה through the idea of contraction in anguish); to approach; hence, to meet in various senses; befall, deliver, happen, seek a quarrel.

H581.d: (Aramaic) or (feminine) אִנִּיןlemma אֵנִּין first vowel, corrected to אִנִּין; (Aramaic), corresponding to הֵם; they; [idiom] are, them, these.

H582.d: from אָנַשׁ; properly, a mortal (and thus differing from the more dignified אָדָם); hence,; a man in general (singly or collectively); another, [idiom] (blood-) thirsty, certain, chap(-man); divers, fellow, [idiom] in the flower of their age, husband, (certain, mortal) man, people, person, servant, some ([idiom] of them), [phrase] stranger, those, [phrase] their trade. It is often unexpressed in the English versions, especially when used in apposition with another word. Compare אִישׁ.

H583.d: the same as אֱנוֹשׁ; Enosh, a son of Seth; Enos.

H584.d: a primitive root; to sigh; groan, mourn, sigh.

H585.d: from אֲנָחָה; sighing; groaning, mourn, sigh.

H586.d: (Aramaic) or אֲנַחְנָה; (Aramaic), corresponding to אֲנַחְנוּ; we; we.

H587.d: apparently from אָנֹכִי; we; ourselves, us, we.

H588.d: probably from the same root as נַחַר; a gorge or narrow pass; Anacharath, a place in Palestine; Anaharath.

H589.d: lemma אֲנַי second vowel, corrected to אֲנִי; contracted from אָנֹכִי; I; I, (as for) me, mine, myself, we, [idiom] which, [idiom] who.

H590.d: probably from אָנָה (in the sense of conveyance); -a ship or (collectively) a fleet; galley, navy (of ships).

H591.d: feminine of אֳנִי; a ship; ship(-men).

H593.d: from אָנָה and עַם; groaning of (the) people; Aniam, an Israelite; Aniam.

H594.d: probably from an unused root meaning to be narrow; according to most a plumb-line, and to others a hook; plumb-line

H595.d: sometimes, aw-no'-kee; a primitive pronoun; I; I, me, [idiom] which.

H596.d: a primitive root; to mourn, i.e. complain; complain.

H598.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אָנַס; figuratively, to distress; trouble.

H599.d: a primitive root; to breathe hard, i.e. be enraged; be angry (displeased).

H600.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אַף (only in the plural as a singular); the face; face, visage.

H601.d: from אָנַף; an unclean bird, perhaps the parrot (from its irascibility); heron.

H602.d: a primitive root; to shriek; cry, groan.

H603.d: from אָנַק; shrieking; crying out, groaning, sighing.

H604.d: the same as אֲנָקָה; some kind of lizard, probably the gecko (from its wail); ferret.

H605.d: a primitive root; to be frail, feeble, or (figuratively) melancholy; desperate(-ly wicked), incurable, sick, woeful.

H606.d: (Aramaic) or אֱנַשׁ; (Aramaic), corresponding to אֱנוֹשׁ; a man; man, [phrase] whosoever.

H607.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אַתָּה; thou; as for thee, thou.

H609.d: of uncertain derivation; Asa, the name of a king and of a Levite; Asa.

H610.d: from סוּךְ; anointed, i.e. an oil-flask; pot.

H612.d: from אָסַר; a bond (especially manacles of a prisoner); band, [phrase] prison.

H613.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אֵסוּר; {a bond (especially manacles of a prisoner)}; band, imprisonment.

H614.d: or אָסִף; from אָסַף; gathered, i.e. (abstractly) a gathering in of crops; ingathering.

H615.d: from אָסַר; bound, i.e. a captive; (those which are) bound, prisoner.

H616.d: for אָסִיר; {bound, i.e. a captive}; prisoner.

H617.d: the same as אַסִּיר; prisoner; Assir, the name of two Israelites; Assir.

H618.d: from an unused root meaning to heap together; a storehouse (only in the plural); barn, storehouse.

H619.d: of uncertain derivation; Asnah, one of the Nethinim; Asnah.

H620.d: of foreign derivation; Osnappar, an Assyrian king; Asnapper.

H621.d: of Egyptian derivation; Asenath, the wife of Joseph; Asenath.

H622.d: a primitive root; to gather for any purpose; hence, to receive, take away, i.e. remove (destroy, leave behind, put up, restore, etc.); assemble, bring, consume, destroy, felch, gather (in, together, up again), [idiom] generally, get (him), lose, put all together, receive, recover (another from leprosy), (be) rereward, [idiom] surely, take (away, into, up), [idiom] utterly, withdraw.

H623.d: from אָסַף; collector; Asaph, the name of three Israelites, and of the family of the first; Asaph.

H624.d: passive participle of אָסַף; collected (only in the plural), i.e. a collection of offerings); threshold, Asuppim.

H625.d: from אָסַף; a collection (of fruits); gathering.

H626.d: from אָסַף; a collection of people (only adverbial); [idiom] together.

H627.d: lemma אֲסֻפָה missing dagesh, corrected to אֲסֻפָּה; feminine of אָסֻף; a collection of (learned) men (only in the plural); assembly.

H628.d: by reduplication from אָסֻף; gathered up together, i.e. a promiscuous assemblage (of people); mixt multitude.

H629.d: (Aramaic) of Persian derivation; diligently; fast, forthwith, speed(-ily).

H630.d: of Persian derivation; Aspatha, a son of Haman; Aspatha.

H631.d: a primitive root; to yoke or hitch; by analogy, to fasten in any sense, to join battle; bind, fast, gird, harness, hold, keep, make ready, order, prepare, prison(-er), put in bonds, set in array, tie.

H632.d: or אִסָּר; from אָסַר; an obligation or vow (of abstinence); binding, bond.

H633.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אֱסָר in a legal sense; an interdict; decree.

H634.d: of foreign derivation; Esar-chaddon, an Assyrian king; Esar-haddon.

H635.d: of Persian derivation; Ester, the Jewish heroine; Esther.

H636.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to עֵץ; a tree or wood; timber, wood.

H637.d: a primitive particle; meaning accession (used as an adverb or conjunction); also or yea; adversatively though; also, [phrase] although, and (furthermore, yet), but, even, [phrase] how much less (more, rather than), moreover, with, yea.

H638.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אַף; {meaning accession (used as an adverb or conjunction); also or yea; adversatively though}; also.

H639.d: from אָנַף; properly, the nose or nostril; hence, the face, and occasionally a person; also (from the rapid breathing in passion) ire; anger(-gry), [phrase] before, countenance, face, [phrase] forebearing, forehead, [phrase] (long-) suffering, nose, nostril, snout, [idiom] worthy, wrath.

H640.d: a primitive root (rather a denominative from אֵפוֹד); to gird on (the ephod); bind, gird.

H641.d: the same as אֵפוֹד shortened; Ephod, an Israelite; Ephod.

H642.d: feminine of אֵפוֹד; a girding on (of the ephod); hence, generally, a plating (of metal); ephod, ornament.

H643.d: apparently of foreign derivation; a pavilion or palace-tent; palace.

H644.d: a primitive root; to cook, especially to bake; bake(-r, (-meats)).

H645.d: or אֵפוֹא; from פֹּה; strictly a demonstrative particle, here; but used of time, now or then; here, now, where?

H646.d: rarely אֵפֹד; probably of foreign derivation; a girdle; specifically the ephod or highpriest's shoulder-piece; also generally, an image; ephod.

H647.d: perhaps from פּוּחַ; breeze; Aphiach, an Israelite; Aphiah.

H648.d: from the same as אָפֵל (in the sense of weakness); unripe; not grown up.

H649.d: dual of אַף; two nostrils; Appajim, an Israelite; Appaim.

H650.d: from אָסַף; properly, containing, i.e. a tube; also a bed or valley of astream; also a strong thing or a hero; brook, channel, mighty, river, [phrase] scale, stream, strong piece.

H651.d: from an unused root meaning to set as the sun; dusky; very dark.

H652.d: from the same as אָפֵל; dusk; darkness, obscurity, privily.

H653.d: feminine of אָפֵל; duskiness, figuratively, misfortune; concrete, concealment; dark, darkness, gloominess, [idiom] thick.

H654.d: from פָּלַל; judge; Ephlal, an Israelite; Ephlal.

H655.d: from an unused root meaning to revolve; a turn, i.e. a season; [phrase] fitly.

H656.d: a primitive root; to disappear, i.e. cease; be clean gone (at an end, brought to nought), fail.

H657.d: from אָפֵס; (sometimes like פָּעַל); cessation, i.e. an end (especially of the earth); often used adverb, no further; also the ankle (in the dual), as being the extremity of the leg or foot; ankle, but (only), end, howbeit, less than nothing, nevertheless (where), no, none (beside), not (any, -withstanding), thing of nought, save(-ing), there, uttermost part, want, without (cause).

H658.d: from אֶפֶס and the plural of דָּם; boundary of blood-drops; Ephes-Dammim, a place in Palestine; Ephes-dammim.

H659.d: from an unused root probably meaning to breathe; properly, a breath, i.e. nothing; of nought.

H660.d: from אֵפַע (in the sense of hissing); an asp or other venomous serpent; viper.

H661.d: a primitive root; to surround; compass.

H662.d: a primitive root; to contain, i.e. (reflex.) abstain; force (oneself), restrain.

H663.d: or אֲפִיק; from אָפַק (in the sense of strength); fortress; Aphek (or Aphik), the name of three places in Palestine; Aphek, Aphik.

H664.d: feminine of אֲפֵק; fortress; Aphekah, a place in Palestine; Aphekah.

H665.d: from an unused root meaning to bestrew; ashes; ashes.

H666.d: from the same as אֵפֶר (in the sense of covering); a turban; ashes.

H667.d: from פָּרַח (in the sense of bursting the shell); the brood of a bird; young (one).

H668.d: probably of Egyptian derivation; a palanquin; chariot.

H669.d: dual of masculine form of אֶפְרָת; double fruit; Ephrajim, a son of Joseph; also the tribe descended from him, and its territory; Ephraim, Ephraimites.

H670.d: (Aramaic) of foreign origin (only in the plural); an Apherasite or inhabitant of an unknown region of Assyria; Apharsite.

H671.d: (Aramaic) or אֲפַרְסַתְכַי; (Aramaic), of foreign origin (only in the plural); an Apharsekite or Apharsathkite, an unknown Assyrian tribe; Apharsachites, Apharasthchites.

H672.d: or אֶפְרָתָה; from פָּרָה; fruitfulness; Ephrath, another name for Bethlehem; once (Psalm 132:6) perhaps for Ephraim; also of an Israelitish woman; Ephrath, Ephratah.

H673.d: patrial from אֶפְרָת; an Ephrathite or an Ephraimite; Ephraimite, Ephrathite.

H674.d: (Aramaic) of Persian origin; revenue; others at the last; revenue.

H675.d: lemma אֶצְבּוֹ missing final nun, corrected to אֶצְבּוֹן; or אֶצְבֹּן; of uncertain derivation; Etsbon, the name of two Israelites; Ezbon.

H676.d: from the same as צֶבַע (in the sense of grasping); something to sieze with, i.e. a finger; by analogy, a toe; finger, toe.

H677.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אֶצְבַּע; {something to sieze with, i.e. a finger; by analogy, a toe}; finger, toe.

H678.d: from אָצַל (in its secondary sense of separation); an extremity (Isaiah 41:9), also a noble; chief man, noble.

H679.d: from אָצַל (in its primary sense of uniting); a joint of the hand (i.e. knuckle); also (according to some) a party-wall (Ezekiel 41:8); (arm) hole, great.

H680.d: a primitive root; properly, to join; used only as a denominative from אֵצֶל; to separate; hence, to select, refuse, contract; keep, reserve, straiten, take.

H681.d: from אָצַל (in the sense of joining); a side; (as a preposition) near; at, (hard) by, (from) (beside), near (unto), toward, with. See also בֵּית הָאֵצֶל.

H682.d: from אָצַל; noble; Atsel, the name of an Israelite, and of a place in Palestine; Azal, Azel.

H683.d: from אָצַל and יָהּ prolonged; Jah has reserved; Atsaljah, an Israelite; Azaliah.

H684.d: from an unused root probably meaning to be strong; strength (i.e. strong); Otsem, the name of two Israelites; Ozem.

H685.d: a variation from צְעָדָה; properly, a step-chain; by analogy, a bracelet; bracelet, chain.

H686.d: a primitive root; to store up; (lay up in) store, [phrase] (make) treasure(-r).

H687.d: from אָצַר; treasure; Etser, an Idumaean; Ezer.

H688.d: from קִדָּה; burning, i.e. a carbuncle or other fiery gem; carbuncle.

H689.d: probably from אָנַק; slender, i.e. the ibex; wild goat.

H690.d: probably for אֲרִי; lion; Ara, an Israelite; Ara.

H691.d: probably for אֲרִיאֵל; a hero (collectively); valiant one.

H692.d: from אֶרְאֵל; heroic; Areli (or an Arelite, collectively), an Israelite and his descendants; Areli, Arelites.

H693.d: a primitive root; to lurk; (lie in) ambush(-ment), lay (lie in) wait.

H694.d: from אָרַב; ambush; Arab, a place in Palestine; Arab.

H695.d: from אָרַב; ambuscade; den, lie in wait.

H697.d: from רָבָה; a locust (from its rapid increase); grasshopper, locust.

H698.d: feminine of אֹרֶב (only in the plural); ambuscades; spoils.

H699.d: feminine participle passive of אָרַב (as if for lurking); a lattice; (by implication) a window, dovecot (because of the pigeon-holes), chimney (with its apertures for smoke), sluice (with openings for water); chimney, window.

H700.d: plural of אֲרֻבָּה; Arubboth, a place in Palestine; Aruboth.

H701.d: patrial from אֲרָב; an Arbite or native of Arab; Arbite.

H702.d: masculine אַרְבָּעָה; from רָבַע; four; four.

H704.d: the same as אַרְבַּע; Arba, one of the Anakim; Arba.

H707.d: a primitive root; to plait or weave; weaver(-r).

H708.d: from אָרַג; a weaving; a braid; also a shuttle; beam, weaver's shuttle.

H709.d: from the same as רֶגֶב; stony; Argob, a district of Palestine; Argob.

H710.d: a variation for אַרְגָּמָן; purple; purple.

H712.d: perhaps from רָגַז (in the sense of being suspended),; a box (as a pannier); coffer.

H713.d: of foreign origin; purple (the color or the dyed stuff); purple.

H714.d: from an unused root probably meaning to wander; fugitive; Ard, the name of two Israelites; Ard.

H715.d: from the same as אַרְדְּ; roaming; Ardon, an Israelite; Ardon.

H716.d: patronymic from אַרְדְּ; an Ardite (collectively) or descendant of Ard; Ardites.

H717.d: a primitive root; to pluck; gather, pluck.

H718.d: (Aramaic) probably akin to אֲלוּ; lo!; behold, lo.

H719.d: probably from רוּד; a refuge for the roving; Arvad, an island-city of Palestine; Arvad.

H720.d: an orthographical variation of אַרְוַד; fugitive; Arod, an Israelite; Arod.

H721.d: patrial from אַרְוַד; an Arvadite or citizen of Arvad; Arvadite.

H722.d: patronymic from אַרְוָדִי; an Arodite or descendant of Arod; Arodi, Arodites.

H723.d: or אֲרָיָה; from אָרָה (in the sense of feeding); a herding-place for an animal; stall.

H724.d: or אֲרֻכָה; feminine passive participle of אָרַךְ (in the sense of restoring to soundness); wholeness (literally or figuratively); health, made up, perfected.

H725.d: a variation of רוּמָה; height; Arumah, a place in Palestine; Arumah.

H726.d: a clerical error for אֱדֹמִי; an Edomite (as in the margin); Syrian.

H727.d: or אָרֹן; from אָרָה (in the sense of gathering); a box; ark, chest, coffin.

H728.d: or (by transposition) אוֹרְנָה; or אַרְנִיָּהlemma אַנִיָּה missing resh, corrected to אַרְנִיָּה; all by orthographical variation for אׇרְנָן; Aravnah (or Arnijah or Ornah), a Jebusite; Araunah.

H729.d: a primitive root; to be firm; used only in the passive participle as a denominative from אֶרֶז; of cedar; made of cedar.

H730.d: from אָרַז; a cedar tree (from the tenacity of its roots); cedar (tree).

H731.d: feminine of אֶרֶז; cedar wainscoating; cedar work.

H732.d: a primitive root; to travel; go, wayfaring (man).

H733.d: from אָרַח; way faring; Arach, the name of three Israelites; Arah.

H734.d: from אָרַח; a well-trodden road (literally or figuratively); also a caravan; manner, path, race, rank, traveller, troop, (by-, high-) way.

H735.d: (Aramaic) corresponding to אֹרַח; a road; way.

H736.d: feminine active participle of אָרַח; a caravan; (travelling) company.

H737.d: feminine passive participle of אָרַח (in the sense of appointing); a ration of food; allowance, diet, dinner, victuals.

H738.d: or (prolonged) [ar-yay']; from אָרָה (in the sense of violence); a lion; (young) lion, [phrase] pierce (from the margin).

H739.d: or אֲרִאֵל; from אֲרִי and אֵל; lion of God; i.e. heroic; lionlike men.

H740.d: xlit ʼĂrîʼêl corrected to ʼĂrîyʼêl; the same as אֲרִיאֵל; Ariel, a symbolical name for Jerusalem, also the name of an Israelite; Ariel.

H741.d: either by transposition for אֲרִיאֵל or, more probably, an orthographical variation for הַרְאֵל; the altar of the temple; altar.

H742.d: of Persian origin; Aridai, a son of Haman; Aridai.

H743.d: of Persian origin; Aridatha, a son of Haman; Aridatha.

H745.d: the same as אֲרִי; lion; Arjeh, an Israelite; Arieh.

H746.d: of foreign origin; Arjok, the name of two Babylonians; Arioch.

H747.d: of Persian origin; Arisai, a son of Haman; Arisai.

H748.d: a primitive root; to be (causative, make) long (literally or figuratively); defer, draw out, lengthen, (be, become, make, pro-) long, [phrase] (out-, over-) live, tarry (long).

H749.d: (Aramaic) properly, corresponding to אָרַךְ, but used only in the sense of reaching to a given point; to suit; be meet.

H750.d: from אָרַךְ; long; long(-suffering, -winged), patient, slow (to anger).

H751.d: from אָרַךְ; length; Erek, a place in Babylon; Erech.

H753.d: from אָרַךְ; length; [phrase] forever, length, long.

H754.d: (Aramaic) or אַרְכָּה; (Aramaic), from אֲרַךְ; length; lengthening, prolonged.

H755.d: (Aramaic) from an unused root corresponding to רָכַב (in the sense of bending the knee); the knee; knee.

H756.d: (Aramaic) patrial from אֶרֶךְ; an Arkevite (collectively) or native of Erek; Archevite.

H757.d: patrial from another place (in Palestine) of similar name with אֶרֶךְ; an Arkite or native of Erek; Archi, Archite.

H758.d: from the same as אַרְמוֹן; the highland; Aram or Syria, and its inhabitants; also the name of the son of Shem, a grandson of Nahor, and of an Israelite; Aram, Mesopotamia, Syria, Syrians.

H759.d: from an unused root (meaning to be elevated); a citadel (from its height); castle, palace. Compare הַרְמוֹן.

H760.d: xlit ʼĂram Tsôbâh corrected to ʼĂram Tsôwbâh; from אֲרָם and צוֹבָא; Aram of Tsoba (or Coele-Syria); Aram-zobah.

H761.d: patrial from אֲרָם; an Aramite or Aramaean; Syrian, Aramitess.

H762.d: feminine of אֲרַמִּי; (only adverbial) in Aramean; in the Syrian language (tongue), in Syriac.

H763.d: from אֲרָם and the dual of נָהָר; Aram of (the) two rivers (Euphrates and Tigris) or Mesopotamia; Aham-naharaim, Mesopotamia.

H764.d: from אַרְמוֹן; palatial; Armoni, an Israelite; Armoni.

H765.d: from רָנַן; stridulous; Aran, an Edomite; Aran.

H766.d: from the same as אֲרָן (in the sense of strength); the ash tree (from its toughness); ash.

H767.d: the same as אֹרֶן; Oren, an Israelite; Oren.

H768.d: of uncertain derivation; the hare; hare.
